The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Yellowing/chlorosis concentrated at the margins and lower leaf
- Dark brown to black necrotic areas at the tip and upper margins
- Green tissue preserved along the central vein
- Overall pattern suggests a marginal/vascular disease

This strongly resembles **Verticillium Wilt** (V-shaped lesions, marginal yellowing, necrosis). Let me confirm with a reference image.

The reference image confirms the pattern: V-shaped brown necrotic lesions surrounded by yellow chlorosis at the leaf margins, matching the test image closely.

**Analysis:**
- Test image: tomato leaf with marginal yellowing, dark brown/black necrosis at the tip and upper margins, green tissue preserved along central vein
- Reference (Verticillium Wilt): identical V-shaped necrosis with yellow chlorosis border
- The description matches: "V-shaped leaf lesions widest at the leaf margin, brown necrotic tissue surrounded by irregular yellowing"
- Rules out Late Blight (no water-soaked greasy appearance, no white fuzzy growth), Early Blight (no concentric rings), and Septoria (no small circular spots)
